metadata.question: Did Washington D.C. experience an air temperature difference of at least 24 degrees Celcius between January 29 and February 5, 2019?

data.raw_code: The question asks about air temperature difference in Washington D.C. between January 29 and February 5, 2019. I need to: 1. Get temperature data for both dates 2. Use a reliable temperature dataset (ERA5 would be good for this) 3. Calculate the difference and check if it's ≥24°C Strategy: - Use ERA5-Land hourly data for temperature - Define Washington D.C. as a point geometry - Get temperature for January 29, 2019 and February 5, 2019 - Calculate mean temperature for each day - Compute difference and check if ≥24°C Potential issues: - No data for those specific dates (C1) - Invalid temperature values (C3) - Valid pixels should be fine since ERA5 has global coverage I'll use ERA5-Land which has temperature_2m band. ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const washingtonDC = ee.Geometry.Point([-77.0369, 38.9072]); // Define date ranges for each day const jan29 = ee.Date('2019-01-29'); const feb5 = ee.Date('2019-02-05'); // 2. Data Acquisition - ERA5-Land for temperature const era5Temp = ee.ImageCollection('ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/HOURLY') .select('temperature_2m'); // Get images for January 29 const jan29Collection = era5Temp .filterDate(jan29, jan29.advance(1, 'day')) .filterBounds(washingtonDC); // Get images for February 5 const feb5Collection = era5Temp .filterDate(feb5, feb5.advance(1, 'day')) .filterBounds(washingtonDC); // Check collection sizes const jan29Size = jan29Collection.size().getInfo(); const feb5Size = feb5Collection.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Jan 29 Images: ${jan29Size}, Feb 5 Images: ${feb5Size}`); if (jan29Size === 0 || feb5Size === 0) { console.log("C1"); return; } // Calculate mean temperature for each day const jan29Mean = jan29Collection.mean(); const feb5Mean = feb5Collection.mean(); // Get temperature values const jan29Temp = jan29Mean.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: washingtonDC, scale: 1000 }).get('temperature_2m'); const feb5Temp = feb5Mean.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: washingtonDC, scale: 1000 }).get('temperature_2m'); // Get pixel count for validation const pixelCount = jan29Mean.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.count(), geometry: washingtonDC, scale: 1000 }).get('temperature_2m'); const jan29Val = jan29Temp.getInfo(); const feb5Val = feb5Temp.getInfo(); const count = pixelCount.getInfo(); console.log(`Jan 29 Temp: ${jan29Val ? jan29Val.toFixed(2) : 'N/A'}°C`); console.log(`Feb 5 Temp: ${feb5Val ? feb5Val.toFixed(2) : 'N/A'}°C`); console.log(`Valid pixels: ${count}`); // 5. Validation & Final Answer if (jan29Val === null || feb5Val === null || isNaN(jan29Val) || isNaN(feb5Val) || count === 0) { console.log("C3"); return; } const tempDiff = Math.abs(jan29Val - feb5Val); console.log(`Temperature difference: ${tempDiff.toFixed(2)}°C`); if (tempDiff >= 24) { console.log("A"); } else { console.log("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
